exposure: None. This seat's method (D6.md) reads only README.md, DISCLAIMER.md, manifest.json, hacs.json, services.yaml, strings.json and translations/*, none of which are audit-era documents.

findings.title: README Requirements section omits threadpoolctl, an actual manifest.json/runtime dependency
findings.claim: README.md's "## Requirements" section states the Python dependencies as "`numpy` and `scipy`, installed automatically from the integration manifest", but manifest.json's `requirements` list also pins `threadpoolctl>=3.5.0`, which is resolved by name and used at runtime in optimizer.py (comment at optimizer.py:265: "Resolved by name, not imported: threadpoolctl publishes no py.typed..."), and README never names it anywhere in the Requirements section.

evidence.machine: cloud 4-vCPU container (see BASELINE.md); this is a pure text/AST scan (count), not a timing number, so contention-immune
evidence.contention_note: box shared with up to 13 other seats; irrelevant to this count metric

perturbation.change: Remove the `threadpoolctl>=3.5.0` entry from manifest.json's `requirements` list (done and reverted during this measurement; tree restored byte-identical to baseline afterwards) and re-run the harness.

findings.metric_definition: Count of manifest.json requirements package names absent from README's Requirements prose AND found by literal string in production *.py (a real runtime dep).
findings.phenomenon_property: any package manifest.json pins in `requirements` and that production code resolves by name is absent from README's Requirements prose; enumerate with `python3 tools/audit/round8/D6/s1_requirements_claim.py`, which lists every such package in `undocumented_and_used_count`
findings.proposed_fix_scope: One-line addition to README.md's "## Requirements" bullet list naming threadpoolctl (e.g. "`numpy`, `scipy` and `threadpoolctl`, installed automatically from the integration manifest"). No production code change; no golden drift expected.
